     9	
    10	- **T1 — connections are open.** A connection is a bidirectional
    11	  opening between two rooms with exactly one endpoint cell in each. No
    12	  state, no locks, no Interact. Door state is a future wave.
    13	- **T2 — traversal is standing at the threshold.** `Traverse` requires
    14	  the member's position to equal the connection's endpoint in the
    15	  member's current room; the member arrives at the far endpoint in the
    16	  other room. Anything else is `ErrBadPlacement`.
    17	- **T3 — sight never crosses a connection.** Percept computation
    18	  remains room-scoped. An opening is not a window.
    19	- **T4 — traversal is an activity, not time.** Like `Move`, `Traverse`
    20	  never advances the clock. Only `Pump` advances the clock.
    21	- **T5 — deciders know self, holdings, and the map; never live truth.**
    22	  The decide phase receives the decider's own room + position and its
    23	  holdings. Static topology may be given to a decider at construction.
    24	  C2 stands: nothing about other members' current state ever reaches a
    25	  decider except through its own holdings.
    26	
    27	## Type changes
    28	
    29	```go
    30	// RoomInput gains a grid choice. Zero value is GridShapeSquare —
    31	// existing setups, tests, and goldens are untouched. Hex rooms make
    32	// the dungeon-absolute hex wire projection an identity mapping.
    33	type RoomInput struct {
    34		// ... existing fields ...
    35		Grid spatial.GridShape // square (default) | hex | gridless
    36	}
    37	// In-bounds validation (member placement, connection endpoints,
    38	// movement targets) defers to the constructed grid's own validity
    39	// check; the module owns no rectangle math of its own.
    40	
    41	// ConnectionInput gains endpoints (BREAKING for stored v0.1 data that
    42	// declared connections — none exists; rpg-api is not wired yet).
    43	type ConnectionInput struct {
    44		ID string
    45		From string                 // room ID
    46		FromPosition spatial.Position // endpoint cell in From
    47		To string                   // room ID
    48		ToPosition spatial.Position   // endpoint cell in To
    49	}
    50	
    51	// TraverseInput follows the family signature law.
    52	type TraverseInput struct {
    53		Member     MemberID
    54		Connection string // ConnectionInput.ID
    55	}
    56	
    57	// TraverseOutput mirrors MoveOutput: deltas, never published; Outcome
    58	// present iff the arrival closed the encounter.
    59	type TraverseOutput struct { /* same shape family as MoveOutput */ }
    60	
    61	// Snapshot is what a decider decides from. Replaces the bare holdings
    62	// slice (interface change; zero external implementors).
    63	type Snapshot struct {
    64		Room     string
    65		Position spatial.Position
    66		Holdings []intel.Holding
    67	}
    68	
    69	type Decider interface {
    70		Decide(snap Snapshot) (Intent, error)
    71	}
    72	
    73	// IntentTraverse joins IntentMoveTo and IntentHold.
    74	type IntentTraverse struct {
    75		Connection string
    76	}
    77	```
    78	
    79	## Verb surface
    80	
    81	| Verb | Change |
    82	|---|---|
    83	| `Traverse(*TraverseInput) (*TraverseOutput, error)` | NEW. Precondition per T2. Refreshes percepts in **both** rooms (departure and arrival are observable absences/appearances). Appends a `traversed` beat. Runs ending evaluation at the arrival position. Rejects on `ErrClosed`, `ErrNilInput`, `ErrNoMember`, `ErrNoConnection`, `ErrBadPlacement`. |
    84	| `Move` | Unchanged, still same-room; its doc comment stays honest about that. |
    85	| `Pump` | Phase 2 executes `IntentTraverse` with the same T2 precondition. Failure contract (corrected during Task 3 to match the module's shipped v0.1 semantics): a phase-1 decider ERROR aborts the pump atomically (R5 — clock untouched, no beats, nothing executed); a phase-2 EXECUTION failure (illegal position, unknown connection) is silently skipped — the pump completes, and that action is simply absent from output and beats — exactly like a failed `IntentMoveTo` has always behaved. |
    86	| `View`, `Story`, `Join`, `Exit`, `End`, `ToData`/`LoadEncounter` | Unchanged surfaces; behavior notes below. |
    87	
    88	New sentinel: `ErrNoConnection` (unknown connection ID), wrapped
    89	multi-`%w` like the family's other sentinels and pinned by `errors.Is`.
    90	
    91	## Validation (Setup and Load — same rules, one-defect fixtures)
    92	
    93	Reject when: duplicate connection ID; `From`/`To` names an unknown
    94	room; `From == To` (self-connection); an endpoint out of the room's
    95	bounds; an endpoint on an occluder. Load-side violations wrap
    96	`ErrInvalidData` multi-`%w` with discriminating message fragments, in
    97	the wave-1 `validEncounterData()` one-defect table style. Every new
    98	field appears in the rich golden (`TestGoldenJSONRich` grows
    99	connections with both endpoints).
   100	
   101	## Persistence
   102	
   103	`FieldData` already persists construction inputs; connections gain
   104	their endpoint fields in the blob. Reload pins: a member who traversed
   105	reloads in the **new** room (construct-path reload preserves member
   106	room, not connection history); ordered iteration stays deterministic
   107	(C8 — connections sorted by ID wherever order is observable).
   108	
   109	## Decider flow (the point of the wave)
   110	
   111	A goblin standing in the crypt saw alice slip through the north opening
   112	last tick. Its holdings contain a ghost whose `SightPayload.Room` says
   113	`hall`. Constructed with the map, it knows `north-door` leads there. It
   114	decides `IntentTraverse{Connection: "north-door"}`; phase 2 executes;
   115	its percepts refresh in the hall; the chase is on. This must exist as
   116	an integration pin (the wave's vandalDecider analogue): decider crosses
   117	a room boundary in pursuit of a ghost, using only self + holdings + the
   118	map it was built with.
   119	
   120	## Compatibility notes (honest, both acceptable at zero consumers)
   121	
   122	1. Stored v0.1 blobs that declared connections fail v0.2 load
   123	   (endpoints required). No such blobs exist outside this repo's own
   124	   fixtures.
   125	2. `Decider` implementors must adopt `Snapshot`. The only implementors
   126	   live in this module's tests and workbench.
   127	
   128	`gorelease` gate stays in CI; tag `rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/v0.2.0`.
   129	
   130	Wire-shape amendments (Copilot round on PR #924, ratified): the blob
   131	persists grid shape as a **string** using spatial's own serialization
   132	vocabulary (`GridTypeHex`/`GridTypeGridless`; empty = square), never
   133	the iota integer — constant reordering must not reinterpret stored
   134	data. Connection endpoints persist as pointers with **presence
   135	required at load** (nil → ErrInvalidData+ErrBadConnection naming the
   136	side) — a missing endpoint must reject, not silently become the legal
   137	cell (0,0). This is what makes compat note 1 above genuinely true.
   138	
   139	Coordinate-model amendment (Kirk, 2026-08-11, ratified): **hex rooms
   140	speak axial/cube, not offset.** `buildRoomGrid` constructs spatial's
   141	`AxialHexGrid` — Position.X/Y are axial Q/R (S = -(Q+R) derived);
   142	bounds are origin-centered spans (negative coordinates legal), unlike
   143	square/gridless's (0,0)-origin rectangles; distance/adjacency/LoS run
   144	the pure cube formulas. Why: the wire and server pathing already speak
   145	cube — axial is cube's lossless 2D projection, so the projection at
   146	the seam is an identity, where the previously-chosen offset HexGrid
   147	would have forced a parity-dependent conversion (the exact confusion
   148	Platform flagged). Side effect: hex validity now diverges from
   149	square's, so the hex tests independently kill the build-square-always
   150	mutant (superseding the earlier "only gridless discriminates"
   151	finding).
   152	
   153	## Acceptance criteria
   154	
   155	- A two-room field with one opening validates, round-trips, and
   156	  rejects each defect class individually with the pinned fragment.
   157	- A player at the threshold traverses; away from it, `ErrBadPlacement`;
   158	  unknown connection, `ErrNoConnection`; after close, `ErrClosed` (the
   159	  sweep grows `Traverse`).
   160	- Traversal triggers ending evaluation: arriving on a
   161	  `TriggerReachedPosition` cell in the destination room closes the
   162	  encounter with the declared key.
   163	- A decider-driven monster pursues a ghost through an opening
   164	  (integration pin above); the pump stays atomic when a traverse
   165	  intent's precondition fails.
   166	- Percepts: departure room observers lose Current status on the
   167	  traverser (ghost forms at the threshold); arrival room observers gain
   168	  Current; sight does not cross the opening in either direction (T3
   169	  pin: observer adjacent to an endpoint sees nothing in the far room).
   170	- Scene test tells one continuous story ending in a cross-room event;
   171	  the wave-1 tombwatch scene and its archived transcript stay
   172	  untouched.
   173	- The module Example gains (or a sibling Example adds) a pinned
   174	  transcript showing a traversal beat; `./scripts/verify.sh
   175	  rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter` prints it.

     1	# Encounter transitions — brainstorm (wave 2 of the free-roam composition)
     2	
     3	Issue: #922. Builds on `docs/ideas/encounter/` (wave 1, shipped as
     4	`rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/v0.1.0`, PR #921). Ratified conversationally
     5	with Kirk on 2026-08-10; this document records the decisions and his
     6	words that shaped them.
     7	
     8	## The forcing question
     9	
    10	rpg-api#793 wires the composition into the game as a coexisting
    11	encounter type. The wire speaks one dungeon-absolute space — a
    12	deliberate choice: *"we left that per room because it put load on the
    13	web to connect and build dungeons from separate rooms."* And movement
    14	crosses rooms: *"pathing goes from room to room."* The composition's
    15	`Move` is same-room by documented v1 constraint, and wave 1's
    16	`ConnectionInput{ID, From, To}` is declared but inert. Multi-room free
    17	roam blocks on giving that topology teeth.
    18	
    19	## Decisions
    20	
    21	### 1. The composition owns the topology (confirmed, not new)
    22	
    23	Wave 1 already put connections in `FieldInput`; v0.2 makes them do
    24	something. The alternative — an adapter-only `Transfer` verb where
    25	rpg-api decides what's traversable — was rejected because deciders live
    26	at the composition level: if the composition doesn't know rooms
    27	connect, **a monster can never chase a player through a doorway**.
    28	Pursuit would die at every room boundary, capping monster behavior at
    29	single-room forever and quietly moving rules truth (what is
    30	traversable) out of the rulebook.
    31	
    32	### 2. Openings only — no door state
    33	
    34	Kirk: *"our freeroam can open doors and it can actually be simplified
    35	if that helps us. we can get there when we get there."* The live game's
    36	door interaction is explicitly not a parity requirement. Connections in
    37	v0.2 are always-open openings. Door state (open/closed/locked,
    38	Interact semantics, probably interrupt windows) is a later wave.
    39	
    40	### 3. Sight stays room-scoped
    41	
    42	Connections do not transmit line of sight in this version. Crossing a
    43	boundary is how you learn what's there — good dungeon-crawl texture,
    44	and it keeps v0.2 from inheriting surprise cross-room occlusion math.
    45	Cross-room LoS becomes its own considered feature later, not a freebie.
    46	
    47	### 4. Traversal is an explicit verb, not Move magic
    48	
    49	`Move` stays same-room and honest. A new `Traverse` verb crosses a
    50	connection: the member must be standing at one endpoint; they arrive at
    51	the other. The server already owns pathing in the absolute space, so a
    52	cross-room path decomposes at the adapter into move → traverse → move.
    53	Implicit auto-transition on `Move` was rejected as unfalsifiable magic:
    54	the explicit verb gives a pinnable beat and a crisp precondition.
    55	
    56	### 5. Deciders learn where they stand (resolving the wave-1 gap)
    57	
    58	`Decide(view []intel.Holding)` has no self-placement — flagged at
    59	wave-1 ratification as the View own-placement gap. It bites for real
    60	now: a decider cannot pick a doorway without knowing which room it is
    61	in. v0.2 resolves the gap in the direction the wave-1 design originally
    62	promised: the decider receives a snapshot of its own room + position
    63	alongside its holdings. Static field topology is not secret — deciders
    64	may be constructed knowing the map; what they must never receive is
    65	other members' live truth (C2 stands).
    66	
    67	### 6. Intent vocabulary grows `IntentTraverse`
    68	
    69	Pursuit through an opening is a decision like any other: decided in
    70	phase 1, executed in phase 2, atomic under R5. A goblin that saw you
    71	slip into the hall holds a ghost whose payload names the room — it can
    72	choose the connection that leads there.
    73	
    74	### 7. No dungeon-builder coupling
    75	
    76	Kirk: dungeon builder *"spec 0.4 is not verified and 0.3 is not really
    77	playable."* The composition's authoring surface stays `SetupInput`;
    78	rpg-api's wave-1 dungeon keys use a minimal direct spec. Nothing here
    79	consumes or emits the dungeon-builder pipeline.
    80	
    81	### 8. Rooms choose their grid (added 2026-08-11, Platform pushback)
    82	
    83	Platform flagged the composition's square-grid usage against the
    84	hex-cube wire. The truth: spatial underneath is the same hex engine
    85	the old module ships to the wire (`GridShape`, `NewHexGrid`, cube
    86	coordinates, all LoS/adjacency behind the Grid interface); the
    87	composition merely *chose* square at its two grid-construction sites.
    88	v0.2 makes the choice per-room: `RoomInput` gains a `GridShape`
    89	(zero value = square, fully compatible), and in-bounds validation
    90	defers to the grid's own validity check instead of rectangle math.
    91	Rooms constructed hex make the wire projection identity rather than a
    92	lossy square→hex remap.
    93	
    94	### 9. Version and compatibility
    95	
    96	`v0.2.0`, additive in spirit. Two honest compat notes, both acceptable
    97	at zero external consumers (rpg-api is not wired yet): connection
    98	validation tightens (endpoints become required), and the `Decider`
    99	interface signature changes. Both are called out in the design.
   100	
   101	## Shelved (future us answers better than today us)
   102	
   103	- Door state, locks, and their Interact/interrupt semantics.
   104	- Cross-room line of sight through openings.
   105	- One-way or conditional connections (chutes, portcullises).
   106	- Combat chaining at a doorway (rides #916).

--- encounter traverse+join 740-1180 ---
   740	
   741		// Move the entity between rooms via spatial's purpose-built transition
   742		// seam: TransitionEntity removes from the source room (the SAME
   743		// registry cleanup RemoveEntity performs — the wave-1 Exit lesson
   744		// applies here too) and, as a backstop behind our own checks above,
   745		// independently re-validates against spatial's own bookkeeping that
   746		// the connection exists, actually links these two rooms (in either
   747		// direction, since door connections are Reversible), and the entity
   748		// was truly indexed in the departure room. TransitionEntity
   749		// deliberately does NOT place the entity — PlaceEntity must always
   750		// follow, using the SAME entity value TransitionEntity returned.
   751		transitioned, err := e.orchestrator.TransitionEntity(&spatial.TransitionEntityInput{
   752			EntityID:     core.EntityID(member.ID),
   753			FromRoom:     spatial.RoomID(fromRoom),
   754			ToRoom:       spatial.RoomID(toRoom),
   755			ConnectionID: spatial.ConnectionID(connectionID),
   756		})
   757		if err != nil {
   758			return traverseResult{}, fmt.Errorf("transition entity: %w: %w", ErrBadPlacement, err)
   759		}
   760	
   761		// LIMBO WINDOW (defensive, currently unreachable): if PlaceEntity below
   762		// were to fail after TransitionEntity above already succeeded, the
   763		// entity would be removed from every room and placed in none — this
   764		// function does not roll back. Four invariants keep that window
   765		// unreachable today: (1) rooms are immutable after Setup/Load, so
   766		// fromRoom/toRoom always exist; (2) member entities never block
   767		// placement (memberEntity.BlocksMovement() is always false), so
   768		// occupancy can never reject PlaceEntity; (3) connection endpoints are
   769		// grid-validated at both entry seams (Setup and Load), so toPos is
   770		// always valid on the arrival room's grid; (4) door connections are
   771		// permanently Passable and Reversible (CreateDoorConnection, never
   772		// mutated after Setup/Load), so TransitionEntity's own passability and
   773		// direction checks always agree with ours. A future change that
   774		// violates any one of these must meet this comment as a deliberate
   775		// decision point, not a silent atomicity regression.
   776		_, err = e.orchestrator.PlaceEntity(&spatial.PlaceEntityInput{
   777			RoomID:   spatial.RoomID(toRoom),
   778			Entity:   transitioned.Entity,
   779			Position: toPos,
   780		})
   781		if err != nil {
   782			return traverseResult{}, fmt.Errorf("place entity: %w: %w", ErrBadPlacement, err)
   783		}
   784	
   785		member.Room = toRoom
   786	
   787		return traverseResult{fromRoom: fromRoom, fromPos: fromPos, toRoom: toRoom, toPos: toPos}, nil
   788	}
   789	
   790	// Traverse moves a member across a connection from their current endpoint to
   791	// the connection's OTHER endpoint, in the other room. Validation order (R5
   792	// atomicity): nil input → closed → not a member → traverseMember's own
   793	// checks (connection not found: ErrNoConnection; endpoint mismatch — wrong
   794	// room or wrong position, either rejects the same way: ErrBadPlacement).
   795	//
   796	// The clock is NOT advanced — traversal is an activity, not time (law T4).
   797	// Sight refreshes for ALL members in one refreshSight call: since
   798	// refreshSight scopes each observer's percept to members currently in
   799	// THEIR OWN room, updating member.Room before the refresh (done inside
   800	// traverseMember) is sufficient — departure-room observers naturally stop
   801	// seeing the traverser (intel's existing complete-percept contract ghosts
   802	// them at their last-known position, the departure endpoint) and
   803	// arrival-room observers naturally gain them Current. No per-room
   804	// special-casing needed, and sight cannot cross the opening in either
   805	// direction: rooms are separate spatial containers with no shared
   806	// geometry (spatial ADR-0015), so there is no code path by which an
   807	// observer's line-of-sight computation — scoped entirely to entities in
   808	// their own room — could see into the other room.
   809	//
   810	// Ending evaluation mirrors Move exactly, evaluated against the ARRIVAL
   811	// room/position: unfiltered ReachedPosition triggers fire for player
   812	// members only; member-filtered triggers fire for the named member
   813	// regardless of kind.
   814	func (e *Encounter) Traverse(in *TraverseInput) (*TraverseOutput, error) {
   815		// Validation order
   816		if in == nil {
   817			return nil, fmt.Errorf("traverse: %w", ErrNilInput)
   818		}
   819	
   820		if e.outcome != nil {
   821			return nil, fmt.Errorf("traverse: %w", ErrClosed)
   822		}
   823	
   824		member, ok := e.members[in.Member]
   825		if !ok {
   826			return nil, fmt.Errorf("traverse: %w", ErrNotMember)
   827		}
   828	
   829		result, err := e.traverseMember(member, in.Connection)
   830		if err != nil {
   831			return nil, fmt.Errorf("traverse: %w", err)
   832		}
   833	
   834		memberIDs := make([]MemberID, 0, len(e.members))
   835		for id := range e.members {
   836			memberIDs = append(memberIDs, id)
   837		}
   838		sort.Slice(memberIDs, func(i, j int) bool { return memberIDs[i] < memberIDs[j] })
   839	
   840		intelDeltas, err := e.refreshSight(memberIDs)
   841		if err != nil {
   842			return nil, fmt.Errorf("traverse refresh sight: %w", err)
   843		}
   844	
   845		// Record the traversal beat. The clock is NOT advanced (law T4).
   846		clockReadingInt := e.clock.ToData().HighWater
   847		clockReadingForBeat := uint64(clockReadingInt)
   848		beatPayload := map[string]interface{}{
   849			"beat":       "traversed",
   850			"member":     string(in.Member),
   851			"connection": in.Connection,
   852			"room":       result.toRoom,
   853			"position":   result.toPos,
   854		}
   855		beatBytes, _ := json.Marshal(beatPayload)
   856	
   857		appendOut, err := e.story.Append(&record.AppendInput{
   858			At:       clockReadingForBeat,
   859			Audience: memberIDs,
   860			Tags:     map[string]string{"tag": "movement"},
   861			Payload:  beatBytes,
   862		})
   863		if err != nil {
   864			return nil, fmt.Errorf("traverse append beat: %w", err)
   865		}
   866	
   867		seqNum := appendOut.Seq
   868	
   869		// Evaluate ReachedPosition endings against the ARRIVAL room/position.
   870		var firedOutcome *Outcome
   871		for _, de := range e.endings {
   872			endingKey, trigger := de.key, de.trigger
   873			reachedPosTrigger, ok := trigger.(TriggerReachedPosition)
   874			if !ok {
   875				continue // Not a ReachedPosition trigger
   876			}
   877	
   878			if reachedPosTrigger.Room != result.toRoom {
   879				continue // Different room
   880			}
   881	
   882			if reachedPosTrigger.Position.X != result.toPos.X || reachedPosTrigger.Position.Y != result.toPos.Y {
   883				continue // Different position
   884			}
   885	
   886			// Check member filter: empty = any player member; non-empty = specific member
   887			if reachedPosTrigger.Member != "" && reachedPosTrigger.Member != in.Member {
   888				continue // Member filter doesn't match
   889			}
   890	
   891			// Member filter passes (empty or matches) but we need to check kind
   892			if reachedPosTrigger.Member == "" && member.Kind != KindPlayer {
   893				continue // Empty filter means players only, but traversing member is not player
   894			}
   895	
   896			// Ending fires! Build the outcome with all members' current positions
   897			memberOutcomes := e.buildMemberOutcomes()
   898	
   899			e.outcome = &Outcome{
   900				Ending:  endingKey,
   901				At:      clockReadingForBeat,
   902				Members: memberOutcomes,
   903			}
   904			// Return a deep copy of the outcome (mutation-proof)
   905			outcomeMembers := make([]MemberOutcome, len(e.outcome.Members))
   906			for i, m := range e.outcome.Members {
   907				outcomeMembers[i] = MemberOutcome{
   908					ID:       m.ID,
   909					Room:     m.Room,
   910					Position: m.Position,
   911				}
   912			}
   913			firedOutcome = &Outcome{
   914				Ending:  e.outcome.Ending,
   915				At:      e.outcome.At,
   916				Members: outcomeMembers,
   917			}
   918			break
   919		}
   920	
   921		return &TraverseOutput{
   922			Traversed: struct {
   923				Member   MemberID
   924				FromRoom string
   925				From     spatial.Position
   926				ToRoom   string
   927				To       spatial.Position
   928			}{
   929				Member:   in.Member,
   930				FromRoom: result.fromRoom,
   931				From:     result.fromPos,
   932				ToRoom:   result.toRoom,
   933				To:       result.toPos,
   934			},
   935			IntelDeltas: intelDeltas,
   936			Seq:         seqNum,
   937			Outcome:     firedOutcome,
   938		}, nil
   939	}
   940	
   941	// Pump advances the world by one tick: the exploration clock advances,
   942	// each monster member (in deterministic order) acts on its own intel via Decider,
   943	// the complete sight refresh happens once, and the story accrues tick and
   944	// move/traverse beats. Errors from a decider abort the pump atomically (R5):
   945	// no clock advance, no moves, no record entries.
   946	//
   947	// Semantics:
   948	//   - Tick advances by exactly 1 (via clock.Advance with displacement 1).
   949	//   - Monsters act in deterministic order (stable Members() order, filtered to KindMonster).
   950	//   - Each decider receives exactly its own Snapshot: own room, own position,
   951	//     own holdings (anti-wall-hack contract C2 — placement included, not just sight).
   952	//   - IntentHold means do nothing; IntentMoveTo executes via the same-room managed
   953	//     seam; IntentTraverse executes via traverseMember (the Traverse verb's own
   954	//     mechanics, shared — see its doc comment).
   955	//   - A spatial rejection of a monster's move, or an illegal traverse intent
   956	//     (unknown connection, or not at the threshold), does NOT abort the pump; the
   957	//     monster simply fails to act. Only a decider error aborts.
   958	//   - After all monster actions: ONE refreshSight for all members, ONE tick beat
   959	//     (stamped with the new clock reading), then move/traverse beats in
   960	//     decision order (the same order monsters were consulted in).
   961	//   - Ending evaluation fires ReachedPosition triggers (only if the filter matches;
   962	//     empty filter = players only, not monsters) against each action's resulting
   963	//     room/position, in the same decision order.
   964	//   - Returns PumpOutput with the new Tick reading, successful moves, successful
   965	//     traverses, deltas, and beats.
   966	func (e *Encounter) Pump(in *PumpInput) (*PumpOutput, error) {
   967		// Validation
   968		if in == nil {
   969			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pump: %w", ErrNilInput)
   970		}
   971	
   972		if e.outcome != nil {
   973			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pump: %w", ErrClosed)
   974		}
   975	
   976		// PHASE 1 — decide. Every decider is consulted BEFORE anything
   977		// mutates: a decider error aborts here with zero state touched
   978		// (R5 — no clock advance, no moves, no beats). This also means a
   979		// later monster's decider error cannot leave an earlier monster's
   980		// move half-applied.
   981		allMembers, err := e.Members()
   982		if err != nil {
   983			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pump members: %w", err)
   984		}
   985	
   986		type plannedAction struct {
   987			memberID MemberID
   988			intent   Intent
   989		}
   990		var planned []plannedAction
   991	
   992		for _, m := range allMembers {
   993			if m.Kind != KindMonster {
   994				continue
   995			}
   996			decider, hasDecider := e.deciders[m.ID]
   997			if !hasDecider {
   998				continue // no decider = hold
   999			}
  1000	
  1001			// The monster's own placement, read fresh from spatial — never
  1002			// another member's. A decider that received anyone else's room or
  1003			// position would be a wall hack extended to placement, not just
  1004			// sight (C2).
  1005			room, ok := e.orchestrator.GetRoom(m.Room)
  1006			if !ok {
  1007				return nil, fmt.Errorf("pump snapshot room: %w", ErrBadPlacement)
  1008			}
  1009			ownPos, ok := room.GetEntityPosition(string(m.ID))
  1010			if !ok {
  1011				return nil, fmt.Errorf("pump snapshot position: %w", ErrBadPlacement)
  1012			}
  1013	
  1014			// The monster's own holdings and nothing else (C2). HeldBy's
  1015			// copy-out is intel's documented contract (pinned in play/intel)
  1016			// — no redundant defensive copy here; the mutating-decider
  1017			// integration test pins the composed guarantee.
  1018			ownHoldings, err := e.intelLog.HeldBy(&intel.HeldByInput{Observer: m.ID})
  1019			if err != nil {
  1020				return nil, fmt.Errorf("pump held_by: %w", err)
  1021			}
  1022	
  1023			intent, err := decider.Decide(Snapshot{Room: m.Room, Position: ownPos, Holdings: ownHoldings})
  1024			if err != nil {
  1025				return nil, fmt.Errorf("pump decide: %w", err)
  1026			}
  1027	
  1028			switch intent.(type) {
  1029			case IntentMoveTo, IntentTraverse:
  1030				planned = append(planned, plannedAction{memberID: m.ID, intent: intent})
  1031			}
  1032		}
  1033	
  1034		// PHASE 2 — execute. Nothing below returns a decider-shaped error;
  1035		// the world now advances.
  1036		_, err = e.clock.Advance(&clock.AdvanceInput{
  1037			Driver:       core.EntityID("world"),
  1038			Displacement: 1,
  1039		})
  1040		if err != nil {
  1041			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pump advance: %w", err)
  1042		}
  1043	
  1044		newTickReading := uint64(e.clock.ToData().HighWater)
  1045	
  1046		// executedAction is built in PLANNED (decision) order regardless of
  1047		// kind, so beats and ending evaluation below stay in the same
  1048		// deterministic per-monster order the deciders were consulted in
  1049		// (C8) — not "all moves then all traverses".
  1050		type executedAction struct {
  1051			member     *Member
  1052			kind       string // "move" or "traverse"
  1053			connection string // only meaningful for "traverse"
  1054			fromRoom   string // only meaningful for "traverse"; a move never changes room
  1055			from       spatial.Position
  1056			toRoom     string // only meaningful for "traverse"
  1057			to         spatial.Position
  1058		}
  1059		var executed []executedAction
  1060	
  1061		for _, p := range planned {
  1062			// The REAL member pointer, not a Members()-derived copy: a
  1063			// traverse mutates member.Room, and that mutation must reach the
  1064			// live e.members entry, not a value copy that planned would
  1065			// otherwise have carried since Setup/Wave-1 (moves never needed
  1066			// to write back Room, so this distinction was previously latent).
  1067			member := e.members[p.memberID]
  1068			if member == nil {
  1069				// A contract-violating decider removed itself from the
  1070				// encounter (e.g. called Exit on its own member) during
  1071				// phase 1's Decide. Its planned action has no live member
  1072				// to execute against — same silent-skip contract as a
  1073				// spatially-rejected move: absent from output and beats,
  1074				// the pump otherwise proceeds normally.
  1075				continue
  1076			}
  1077			switch intent := p.intent.(type) {
  1078			case IntentMoveTo:
  1079				// Spatial rejection does not abort the pump; the monster
  1080				// simply fails to move and no beat is recorded for it.
  1081				fromPos, moveErr := e.moveMember(member, intent.To)
  1082				if moveErr == nil {
  1083					executed = append(executed, executedAction{
  1084						member: member, kind: "move", from: fromPos, to: intent.To,
  1085					})
  1086				}
  1087			case IntentTraverse:
  1088				// An illegal traverse (unknown connection, or not at the
  1089				// threshold) does not abort the pump either — same silent-skip
  1090				// contract as a spatially-rejected move (see traverseMember's
  1091				// doc comment).

  1294			observerPos, ok := room.GetEntityPosition(string(observerID))

  1483	
  1484	// TestTraverseBothDirections pins the threshold-success path in BOTH
  1485	// directions through the same connection (T1 law: connections are
  1486	// bidirectional), asserting room+position after each hop.
  1487	func (s *EncounterTestSuite) TestTraverseBothDirections() {
  1488		s.Run("room-a to room-b", func() {
  1489			enc := s.newTwoRoomEncounterWithConnection()
  1490			out, err := enc.Traverse(&encounter.TraverseInput{Member: alice, Connection: "door1"})
  1491			s.Require().NoError(err)
  1492			s.Equal(alice, out.Traversed.Member)
  1493			s.Equal("room-a", out.Traversed.FromRoom)
  1494			s.Equal(spatial.Position{X: 9, Y: 5}, out.Traversed.From)
  1495			s.Equal("room-b", out.Traversed.ToRoom)
  1496			s.Equal(spatial.Position{X: 0, Y: 5}, out.Traversed.To)
  1497	
  1498			members, err := enc.Members()
  1499			s.Require().NoError(err)
  1500			found := false
  1501			for _, m := range members {
  1502				if m.ID == alice {
  1503					s.Equal("room-b", m.Room)
  1504					found = true
  1505				}
  1506			}
  1507			s.True(found, "alice must still be a member, now in room-b")
  1508		})
  1509	
  1510		s.Run("room-b to room-a (bidirectional through the same connection)", func() {
  1511			enc := s.newTwoRoomEncounterWithConnection()
  1512			_, err := enc.Traverse(&encounter.TraverseInput{Member: alice, Connection: "door1"})
  1513			s.Require().NoError(err)
  1514	
  1515			out, err := enc.Traverse(&encounter.TraverseInput{Member: alice, Connection: "door1"})
  1516			s.Require().NoError(err)
  1517			s.Equal("room-b", out.Traversed.FromRoom)
  1518			s.Equal(spatial.Position{X: 0, Y: 5}, out.Traversed.From)
  1519			s.Equal("room-a", out.Traversed.ToRoom)
  1520			s.Equal(spatial.Position{X: 9, Y: 5}, out.Traversed.To)
  1521	
  1522			members, err := enc.Members()
  1523			s.Require().NoError(err)
  1524			for _, m := range members {
  1525				if m.ID == alice {
  1526					s.Equal("room-a", m.Room)
  1527				}
  1528			}
  1529		})
  1530	}
  1531	
  1532	// TestTraverseGhostAtThreshold pins that a departure-room observer's
  1533	// holding of the traverser fades to a ghost AT THE DEPARTURE ENDPOINT —
  1534	// their last-observed position — not the (never-seen) arrival position.
  1535	func (s *EncounterTestSuite) TestTraverseGhostAtThreshold() {
  1536		enc := s.newTwoRoomEncounterWithConnection()
  1537	
  1538		bobBefore, err := enc.View(&encounter.ViewInput{Member: bob})
  1539		s.Require().NoError(err)
  1540		s.Require().Len(bobBefore, 1, "bob must see alice before the traverse (geometry precondition)")
  1541		s.Equal(intel.Current, bobBefore[0].Status)
  1542	
  1543		_, err = enc.Traverse(&encounter.TraverseInput{Member: alice, Connection: "door1"})
  1544		s.Require().NoError(err)
  1545	
  1546		bobAfter, err := enc.View(&encounter.ViewInput{Member: bob})
  1547		s.Require().NoError(err)
  1548		s.Require().Len(bobAfter, 1, "the ghost is HELD, not gone")
  1549		s.Equal(intel.Held, bobAfter[0].Status, "bob's sight of alice must fade — she left room-a")
  1550	
  1551		var aliceSeen encounter.SightPayload
  1552		s.Require().NoError(json.Unmarshal(bobAfter[0].Payload, &aliceSeen))
  1553		s.Equal("room-a", aliceSeen.Room, "ghost holds alice's LAST-SEEN room")
  1554		s.Equal(9.0, aliceSeen.X, "ghost holds alice at the DEPARTURE endpoint, not the arrival one")
  1555		s.Equal(5.0, aliceSeen.Y)
  1556	}
  1557	
  1558	// TestTraverseArrivalCurrent pins that an arrival-room observer gains the
  1559	// traverser as Current at the arrival endpoint.
  1560	func (s *EncounterTestSuite) TestTraverseArrivalCurrent() {
  1561		enc := s.newTwoRoomEncounterWithConnection()
  1562	
  1563		_, err := enc.Traverse(&encounter.TraverseInput{Member: alice, Connection: "door1"})
  1564		s.Require().NoError(err)
  1565	
  1566		goblinView, err := enc.View(&encounter.ViewInput{Member: goblin})
  1567		s.Require().NoError(err)
  1568		s.Require().Len(goblinView, 1)
  1569		s.Equal(intel.Subject(alice), goblinView[0].Subject)
  1570		s.Equal(intel.Current, goblinView[0].Status, "goblin must see alice as Current — she arrived in room-b")
  1571	
  1572		var aliceSeen encounter.SightPayload
  1573		s.Require().NoError(json.Unmarshal(goblinView[0].Payload, &aliceSeen))
  1574		s.Equal("room-b", aliceSeen.Room)

  1576		s.Equal(5.0, aliceSeen.Y)
  1577	}

  1580	// connection's opening. goblin stands in room-b, adjacent to the arrival
  1581	// endpoint. Before alice traverses — while she's still in room-a, at the
  1582	// connection's OTHER endpoint — goblin must have NO holding of her at

  1587	func (s *EncounterTestSuite) TestTraverseSightNeverCrossesOpening() {

  1590		goblinBefore, err := enc.View(&encounter.ViewInput{Member: goblin})

  1595	// TestTraverseOwnView pins that after traversing, the traverser's OWN
  1596	// percept reflects arrival-room members Current and departure-room
  1597	// members faded to ghosts — the same complete-percept contract that
  1598	// governs everyone else's view of them.
  1599	func (s *EncounterTestSuite) TestTraverseOwnView() {
  1600		enc := s.newTwoRoomEncounterWithConnection()
  1601	
  1602		aliceBefore, err := enc.View(&encounter.ViewInput{Member: alice})
  1603		s.Require().NoError(err)
  1604		s.Require().Len(aliceBefore, 1, "alice sees only bob before traversing (goblin is behind the unopened door)")
  1605		s.Equal(intel.Subject(bob), aliceBefore[0].Subject)
  1606		s.Equal(intel.Current, aliceBefore[0].Status)
  1607	
  1608		_, err = enc.Traverse(&encounter.TraverseInput{Member: alice, Connection: "door1"})
  1609		s.Require().NoError(err)
  1610	
  1611		aliceAfter, err := enc.View(&encounter.ViewInput{Member: alice})
  1612		s.Require().NoError(err)
  1613		s.Require().Len(aliceAfter, 2, "alice now holds both bob (ghosted) and goblin (Current)")
  1614	
  1615		var bobHolding, goblinHolding *intel.Holding
  1616		for i := range aliceAfter {
  1617			switch aliceAfter[i].Subject {
  1618			case intel.Subject(bob):
  1619				bobHolding = &aliceAfter[i]
  1620			case intel.Subject(goblin):
  1621				goblinHolding = &aliceAfter[i]
  1622			}
  1623		}
  1624		s.Require().NotNil(bobHolding, "alice must still hold bob (ghosted)")

  1058	// validEncounterDataWithConnection extends validEncounterData with a second,
  1059	// DELIBERATELY mismatched room (r1 resized to 10x4, r2 added at 3x9) and one
  1060	// fully valid connection between them — the base for the connection defect
  1061	// rows below (one-defect discipline: each row breaks exactly one thing about
  1062	// this otherwise-valid connection). FromPosition{7,1} is valid ONLY in r1
  1063	// and ToPosition{1,7} valid ONLY in r2: same-sized rooms and equal From/To
  1064	// positions would make a check that validates an endpoint against the WRONG
  1065	// room (or a From/To transposition in convertConnectionDataToConnectionInput)
  1066	// invisible. r1 carries an occluder at (2,2) and r2 an occluder at (1,3), so
  1067	// both the from- and to-side "endpoint on occluder" rows have something to hit.
  1068	func validEncounterDataWithConnection() encounter.EncounterData {
  1069		d := validEncounterData()
  1070		d.Field.Rooms[0].Width = 10
  1071		d.Field.Rooms[0].Height = 4

  1073		d.Field.Rooms = append(d.Field.Rooms, encounter.RoomData{
  1074			ID: "r2", Width: 3, Height: 9,
  1075			Occluders: []encounter.PositionData{{X: 1, Y: 3}},
  1076		})
  1077		d.Field.Connections = []encounter.ConnectionData{
  1078			{ID: "c1", From: "r1", To: "r2",
  1079				FromPosition: &encounter.PositionData{X: 7, Y: 1},
  1080				ToPosition:   &encounter.PositionData{X: 1, Y: 7}},

    18	// TestVaultChase is the wave's second continuous scene (AC2, alongside
    19	// TestTombWatch — tombwatch itself untouched): ONE flowing story that
    20	// exercises the connection primitives Waves 1's tomb watch predates —
    21	// sight across an open room, slipping through a doorway, the ghost that
    22	// forms at the threshold (not the far side never seen), a mid-chase save/
    23	// reload, a decider's OWN pursuit traverse, an ending declared in the far
    24	// room, and an archive sweep that now includes Traverse. Uses seen() and
    25	// pursuitDecider, shared with tombwatch_test.go and pump_test.go
    26	// respectively (same package).
    27	func TestVaultChase(t *testing.T) {
    28		// ---- The set -----------------------------------------------------
    29		// Two rooms, one gate. DELIBERATELY asymmetric endpoints (T1 review
    30		// lesson): FromPosition {9,5} in the corridor, ToPosition {0,5} in
    31		// the vault — a from/to mix-up would be observable.
    32		const (
    33			corridorRoom    = "corridor"
    34			vaultRoom       = "vault"
    35			gateConnection  = "gate"
    36			sanctuaryEnding = "sanctuary"
    37		)
    38		gate := encounter.ConnectionInput{
    39			ID: gateConnection, From: corridorRoom, To: vaultRoom,
    40			FromPosition: spatial.Position{X: 9, Y: 5},
    41			ToPosition:   spatial.Position{X: 0, Y: 5},
    42		}
    43	
    44		// ---- Beat 1: sight -------------------------------------------------
    45		// Alice and the goblin share the corridor, in the open — first light
    46		// finds them mutually visible. The goblin's pursuitDecider knows the
    47		// gate (static topology, given at construction) and its target
    48		// (alice); it never reads encounter state directly — Snapshot +
    49		// Holdings + its own construction-time config is all it gets (C2).
    50		pursuit := &pursuitDecider{connections: []encounter.ConnectionInput{gate}, target: alice}
    51		enc, err := encounter.NewEncounter(&encounter.SetupInput{
    52			Field: encounter.FieldInput{
    53				Rooms: []encounter.RoomInput{
    54					{ID: corridorRoom, Width: 10, Height: 10},
    55					{ID: vaultRoom, Width: 10, Height: 10},
    56				},
    57				Connections: []encounter.ConnectionInput{gate},
    58			},
    59			Members: []encounter.MemberInput{
    60				{ID: alice, Kind: encounter.KindPlayer, Room: corridorRoom, Position: spatial.Position{X: 2, Y: 5}},
    61				{ID: goblin, Kind: encounter.KindMonster, Room: corridorRoom,
    62					Position: spatial.Position{X: 2, Y: 8}, Decider: pursuit},
    63			},
    64			Endings: []encounter.EndingInput{
    65				{Key: sanctuaryEnding, Trigger: encounter.TriggerReachedPosition{
    66					Room: vaultRoom, Position: spatial.Position{X: 8, Y: 8}}},
    67			},
    68		})
    69		require.NoError(t, err, "beat 1: the corridor assembles")
    70	
    71		st, _ := seen(t, enc, alice, goblin)
    72		require.Equal(t, intel.Current, st, "beat 1: alice sees the goblin across the open corridor")
    73		st, _ = seen(t, enc, goblin, alice)
    74		require.Equal(t, intel.Current, st, "beat 1: and the goblin sees her back — intel is symmetric")
    75	
    76		// ---- Beat 2: to the threshold, and through it ----------------------
    77		// Alice crosses to the gate, then slips through it into the vault.
    78		_, err = enc.Move(&encounter.MoveInput{Member: alice, To: spatial.Position{X: 9, Y: 5}})
    79		require.NoError(t, err, "beat 2: alice crosses to the gate")
    80	
    81		travOut, err := enc.Traverse(&encounter.TraverseInput{Member: alice, Connection: gateConnection})
    82		require.NoError(t, err, "beat 2: she slips through the gate")
    83		require.Equal(t, vaultRoom, travOut.Traversed.ToRoom, "beat 2: she arrives in the vault")
    84		require.Equal(t, spatial.Position{X: 0, Y: 5}, travOut.Traversed.To)
    85	
    86		// The ghost forms — for BOTH of them, symmetrically. Note WHERE:
    87		// the threshold in the corridor, her last-seen position — not the
    88		// vault, which the goblin has never seen at all.
    89		st, p := seen(t, enc, goblin, alice)
    90		require.Equal(t, intel.Held, st, "beat 2: the goblin's sight of alice fades — she left the room")
    91		require.Equal(t, corridorRoom, p.Room, "beat 2: its ghost holds her LAST-SEEN room")
    92		require.Equal(t, 9.0, p.X, "beat 2: at the threshold, not the far side it never saw")
    93		require.Equal(t, 5.0, p.Y)
    94		st, _ = seen(t, enc, alice, goblin)
    95		require.Equal(t, intel.Held, st, "beat 2: alice loses the goblin too — symmetric")
    96	
    97		// She doesn't linger at the arrival cell — she moves deeper into the
    98		// vault, toward (but not yet at) sanctuary.
    99		_, err = enc.Move(&encounter.MoveInput{Member: alice, To: spatial.Position{X: 4, Y: 5}})
   100		require.NoError(t, err, "beat 2: she moves deeper into the vault")
   101	
   102		// ---- Beat 3: the pause (pause is free) ------------------------------
   103		// The table closes the Discord activity mid-chase. The host persists
   104		// ONE aggregate and rehydrates it later. Deciders are behavior, not
   105		// state: the campaign re-attaches a FRESH pursuitDecider at load —
   106		// same topology and target, no memory of its own carried over (its
   107		// INTEL does — beliefs are state and traveled in the aggregate).
   108		data := enc.ToData()
   109		enc2, err := encounter.LoadEncounter(data, map[encounter.MemberID]encounter.Decider{
   110			goblin: &pursuitDecider{connections: []encounter.ConnectionInput{gate}, target: alice},
   111		})
   112		require.NoError(t, err, "beat 3: the suspended chase crosses a process boundary")
   113		enc = enc2 // the reload IS the encounter now

   116		require.Equal(t, intel.Held, st, "beat 3: the ghost survived the reload")
   117		require.Equal(t, corridorRoom, p.Room, "beat 3: still at the threshold — loading never re-derives sight")
   118		require.Equal(t, 9.0, p.X)
   119	
   120		// ---- Beat 4: the pursuit traverse ------------------------------------
   121		// First pump: the goblin, still in the corridor, walks toward the
   122		// ghost's last-seen position — the threshold.
   123		pumpOut1, err := enc.Pump(&encounter.PumpInput{})
   124		require.NoError(t, err, "beat 4: the pursuit resumes")
   125		require.Len(t, pumpOut1.MonsterMoves, 1, "beat 4: the goblin walks toward the threshold")
   126		require.Equal(t, spatial.Position{X: 9, Y: 5}, pumpOut1.MonsterMoves[0].To)
   127		require.Empty(t, pumpOut1.MonsterTraverses, "beat 4: not standing at the threshold yet on this tick's decision")

    76	// buildRoomGrid constructs the spatial Grid for a room's declared shape.
    77	// Called only after validation has confirmed Grid is one of the three known
    78	// GridShape values; the switch's default (square) is therefore unreachable
    79	// in practice and exists only so an unvalidated caller degrades gracefully
    80	// rather than panicking.
    81	//
    82	// Hex rooms build spatial.AxialHexGrid, NOT spatial.HexGrid: the wire (and
    83	// Platform's pathing) speaks cube coordinates natively, and axial (Q, R,
    84	// with S = -(Q+R) derived) is cube's 2D projection — an IDENTITY mapping to
    85	// the wire. HexGrid's bounded offset column/row coordinates would force a
    86	// lossy, orientation-dependent offset<->cube conversion at that seam for no
    87	// benefit inside the composition, which never renders a grid itself.
    88	// width/height become AxialHexGridConfig's SpanWidth/SpanHeight — see
    89	// RoomInput.Grid's doc comment for what that means for a hex room's
    90	// Position values (origin-centered, negative coordinates legal).
    91	func buildRoomGrid(shape spatial.GridShape, width, height int) spatial.Grid {
    92		switch shape {
    93		case spatial.GridShapeHex:
    94			return spatial.NewAxialHexGrid(spatial.AxialHexGridConfig{SpanWidth: float64(width), SpanHeight: float64(height)})
    95		case spatial.GridShapeGridless:
    96			return spatial.NewGridlessRoom(spatial.GridlessConfig{Width: float64(width), Height: float64(height)})
    97		default:
    98			return spatial.NewSquareGrid(spatial.SquareGridConfig{Width: float64(width), Height: float64(height)})
    99		}
   100	}
   328	// IsValidPosition reports true when (Q, R) falls within ±SpanWidth/2 along Q
   329	// and ±SpanHeight/2 along R. The check is centered on the origin because axial
   330	// hex coordinates are symmetric — positions can have negative Q or R. This
   331	// differs from SquareGrid/HexGrid whose bounds start at (0,0).
   332	func (a *AxialHexGrid) IsValidPosition(pos Position) bool {
   333		half := a.dimensions.Width / 2
   334		halfH := a.dimensions.Height / 2
   335		return pos.X >= -half && pos.X < half && pos.Y >= -halfH && pos.Y < halfH
   336	}
   337	
   338	// Distance returns the hex distance between two axial positions.
   339	// Interprets Position.X as Q and Position.Y as R; derives S = -(Q+R).
   340	// Uses the cube formula: (|ΔQ| + |ΔR| + |ΔS|) / 2.
   341	func (a *AxialHexGrid) Distance(from, to Position) float64 {
   342		fromCube := axialToCube(from)
   343		toCube := axialToCube(to)
   344		return float64(fromCube.Distance(toCube))
   474	// axialToCube converts an axial Position (X=Q, Y=R) to a CubeCoordinate.
   475	func axialToCube(pos Position) CubeCoordinate {
   476		q := int(pos.X)
   477		r := int(pos.Y)
   478		return CubeCoordinate{X: q, Y: r, Z: -q - r}
   479	}
   480	
   481	// cubeToAxial converts a CubeCoordinate back to an axial Position (X=Q, Y=R).
   482	func cubeToAxial(c CubeCoordinate) Position {
   483		return Position{X: float64(c.X), Y: float64(c.Y)}

text:
## Verdict: **do not merge #924 as-is**

Reviewed exact GitHub PR range: base `a57f28b79451e2f119d550a35b4a1d2b62f1cff6` → head `41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e` (13 commits; 11 files; +3202/-213), from a clean archive of that head.

### Blockers / high findings

1. **BLOCKER — nil decider reattachment panics on the first Pump.**  
   `LoadEncounter` inserts a map-present `nil` `Decider` into `e.deciders` without validation ([data.go:611–618](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/data.go#L611-L618)). `Pump` treats map presence as a decider and calls `decider.Decide` ([encounter.go:996–1024](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L996-L1024)). Thus `LoadEncounter(data, map[MemberID]Decider{monsterID:nil})` succeeds, then panics.  
   This directly affects #793’s provider-at-load seam. Treat nil as absent/hold or reject it; add the regression test.

2. **HIGH — “identity cube mapping” accepts non-integral positions, then truncates them.**  
   Encounter selects `AxialHexGrid` ([encounter.go:82–98](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L82-L98)). Its published v0.9.0 `IsValidPosition` checks only bounds, so `(-0.5, 0)` is accepted ([hex_grid.go:332–335](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/tools/spatial/v0.9.0/tools/spatial/hex_grid.go#L332-L335)), while cube conversion truncates Q/R via `int` ([hex_grid.go:474–479](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/tools/spatial/v0.9.0/tools/spatial/hex_grid.go#L474-L479)).  
   This is not a total axial/cube-cell model and cannot be an identity projection to integer wire cube coordinates. Enforce integral Q/R at the spatial/hex ingress and cover Setup, Load, Move, and endpoints.

3. **HIGH — returned intel deltas are nondeterministically ordered.**  
   `refreshSight` constructs percepts by ranging `e.members` ([encounter.go:1299–1330](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L1299-L1330)). `intel.Surveil` preserves that input order in public `FirstContact`/`Refreshed` slices ([intel.go:182–211](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/play/intel/intel.go#L182-L211)), which are returned through Move/Traverse/Pump `IntelDeltas`.  
   State/JSON may remain deterministic, but the observable mutation outputs are not. Sort visible subjects before Surveil or make the delta contract explicitly unordered; API stream projection needs the former.

### What is solid

- Connection endpoints are validated at Setup and Load; missing persisted endpoints reject rather than silently becoming `(0,0)` ([data.go:404–433](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/data.go#L404-L433)).
- Grid persistence now uses stable strings, not `GridShape` iotas ([data.go:54–67](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/data.go#L54-L67)).
- Connections and members serialize deterministically by ID ([data.go:120–145](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/data.go#L120-L145)); connections are sorted on both construction/load.
- Traverse correctly uses Spatial’s managed `TransitionEntity` then `PlaceEntity`, and only updates `member.Room` after placement ([encounter.go:751–787](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L751-L787)).
- Pump’s former copied-member aliasing flaw is correctly repaired by live member lookup ([encounter.go:1061–1075](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L1061-L1075)).
- `View` is a pure holdings read; it does not Pump ([encounter.go:398–414](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L398-L414)).

### #793 blocker matrix

| #793 need | #924 status | Evidence / consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-room topology and crossing | **Closed (narrowly)** | Endpoint topology, Traverse, and IntentTraverse are toolkit-owned. |
| Hex support | **Partial** | Axial shape is real, but fractional accepted/truncated positions invalidate a total cube mapping. |
| Per-cell VISIBLE/REMEMBERED View | **Open** | `View` returns only `[]intel.Holding`; it has no cells, room geometry, own position, or total visible/remembered projection. `Member` exposes room but no position ([field.go:181–186](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/field.go#L181-L186)). |
| Stable local↔absolute room mapping | **Partial** | Q/R identity is documented/persisted for authored hex rooms, but no absolute embedding/mapping contract or public projection exists. |
| Traverse/path intent adaptation | **Partial** | Step-level Traverse exists; no target/route verb owns absolute-to-local multi-room decomposition. |
| Decider contribution/re-registration | **Partial** | Non-persistence and reattachment seam are correct, but keyed-nil providers panic. API still must own a provider registry. |
| Event/delta seam | **Partial** | Outputs expose deltas and Story sequences, but deltas lack total cell state and subject ordering is unstable. |
| Reads must not Pump | **Preserved** | View remains a pure read. |

### Release / CI / review

- **`v0.2.0` is the right release class**: the `Decider.Decide` signature is breaking, and pre-v1 minor is the honest Go module version. CI’s `gorelease-dnd5e-encounter` check passed.
- The compatibility narrative is incomplete: adding exported fields to `RoomInput` and `ConnectionInput` also breaks external **unkeyed** composite literals ([field.go:27–57](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/field.go#L27-L57), [71–86](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/field.go#L71-L86)). This does not change the v0.2.0 conclusion, but “one incompatible change” is not fully honest.
- CI is green selectively: changed-module test, ci-status, and Gorelease succeeded; many full/lint jobs were intentionally skipped. Clean-head `go test -race ./...` for the encounter module passed.
- Copilot’s two substantive #924 comments were fixed in `095e6f5`, but both GitHub review threads remain marked unresolved. No approval review decision is recorded.
- #923’s canonical triplet has a stale Task-3 statement saying phase-2 failure atomically aborts ([plan.md:46–53](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/9fa14c5fe47ed7752b94a49087201a3d16ab6f6b/docs/ideas/encounter-transitions/plan.md#L46-L53)); the design and implementation correctly say execution failures skip ([design.md:79–86](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/9fa14c5fe47ed7752b94a49087201a3d16ab6f6b/docs/ideas/encounter-transitions/design.md#L79-L86)). Fix before calling it canonical ratification.

### Thin honest API seam after repairs

API may: load/save the opaque aggregate once, reattach non-nil decider providers, authenticate, call toolkit verbs/Pump on activity, and project toolkit-owned view/change batches.

It cannot honestly yet project the required existing wire knowledge model without inventing semantics: toolkit still needs a total per-cell observer projection plus stable change batch. It also needs a Kirk decision on absolute-route ownership: #793 says API keeps stitching/pathing, but that conflicts with the Boundary Rule if API must choose room transitions/path behavior. #924 provides transition execution, not the route-intent owner.

## Verdict: **do not merge #924 as-is**

Reviewed exact GitHub PR range: base `a57f28b79451e2f119d550a35b4a1d2b62f1cff6` → head `41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e` (13 commits; 11 files; +3202/-213), from a clean archive of that head.

### Blockers / high findings

1. **BLOCKER — nil decider reattachment panics on the first Pump.**  
   `LoadEncounter` inserts a map-present `nil` `Decider` into `e.deciders` without validation ([data.go:611–618](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/data.go#L611-L618)). `Pump` treats map presence as a decider and calls `decider.Decide` ([encounter.go:996–1024](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L996-L1024)). Thus `LoadEncounter(data, map[MemberID]Decider{monsterID:nil})` succeeds, then panics.  
   This directly affects #793’s provider-at-load seam. Treat nil as absent/hold or reject it; add the regression test.

2. **HIGH — “identity cube mapping” accepts non-integral positions, then truncates them.**  
   Encounter selects `AxialHexGrid` ([encounter.go:82–98](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L82-L98)). Its published v0.9.0 `IsValidPosition` checks only bounds, so `(-0.5, 0)` is accepted ([hex_grid.go:332–335](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/tools/spatial/v0.9.0/tools/spatial/hex_grid.go#L332-L335)), while cube conversion truncates Q/R via `int` ([hex_grid.go:474–479](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/tools/spatial/v0.9.0/tools/spatial/hex_grid.go#L474-L479)).  
   This is not a total axial/cube-cell model and cannot be an identity projection to integer wire cube coordinates. Enforce integral Q/R at the spatial/hex ingress and cover Setup, Load, Move, and endpoints.

3. **HIGH — returned intel deltas are nondeterministically ordered.**  
   `refreshSight` constructs percepts by ranging `e.members` ([encounter.go:1299–1330](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L1299-L1330)). `intel.Surveil` preserves that input order in public `FirstContact`/`Refreshed` slices ([intel.go:182–211](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/play/intel/intel.go#L182-L211)), which are returned through Move/Traverse/Pump `IntelDeltas`.  
   State/JSON may remain deterministic, but the observable mutation outputs are not. Sort visible subjects before Surveil or make the delta contract explicitly unordered; API stream projection needs the former.

### What is solid

- Connection endpoints are validated at Setup and Load; missing persisted endpoints reject rather than silently becoming `(0,0)` ([data.go:404–433](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/data.go#L404-L433)).
- Grid persistence now uses stable strings, not `GridShape` iotas ([data.go:54–67](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/data.go#L54-L67)).
- Connections and members serialize deterministically by ID ([data.go:120–145](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/data.go#L120-L145)); connections are sorted on both construction/load.
- Traverse correctly uses Spatial’s managed `TransitionEntity` then `PlaceEntity`, and only updates `member.Room` after placement ([encounter.go:751–787](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L751-L787)).
- Pump’s former copied-member aliasing flaw is correctly repaired by live member lookup ([encounter.go:1061–1075](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L1061-L1075)).
- `View` is a pure holdings read; it does not Pump ([encounter.go:398–414](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/encounter.go#L398-L414)).

### #793 blocker matrix

| #793 need | #924 status | Evidence / consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-room topology and crossing | **Closed (narrowly)** | Endpoint topology, Traverse, and IntentTraverse are toolkit-owned. |
| Hex support | **Partial** | Axial shape is real, but fractional accepted/truncated positions invalidate a total cube mapping. |
| Per-cell VISIBLE/REMEMBERED View | **Open** | `View` returns only `[]intel.Holding`; it has no cells, room geometry, own position, or total visible/remembered projection. `Member` exposes room but no position ([field.go:181–186](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/field.go#L181-L186)). |
| Stable local↔absolute room mapping | **Partial** | Q/R identity is documented/persisted for authored hex rooms, but no absolute embedding/mapping contract or public projection exists. |
| Traverse/path intent adaptation | **Partial** | Step-level Traverse exists; no target/route verb owns absolute-to-local multi-room decomposition. |
| Decider contribution/re-registration | **Partial** | Non-persistence and reattachment seam are correct, but keyed-nil providers panic. API still must own a provider registry. |
| Event/delta seam | **Partial** | Outputs expose deltas and Story sequences, but deltas lack total cell state and subject ordering is unstable. |
| Reads must not Pump | **Preserved** | View remains a pure read. |

### Release / CI / review

- **`v0.2.0` is the right release class**: the `Decider.Decide` signature is breaking, and pre-v1 minor is the honest Go module version. CI’s `gorelease-dnd5e-encounter` check passed.
- The compatibility narrative is incomplete: adding exported fields to `RoomInput` and `ConnectionInput` also breaks external **unkeyed** composite literals ([field.go:27–57](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/field.go#L27-L57), [71–86](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/41412f57bafb40068c50152d6d0fba9387cec60e/rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/field.go#L71-L86)). This does not change the v0.2.0 conclusion, but “one incompatible change” is not fully honest.
- CI is green selectively: changed-module test, ci-status, and Gorelease succeeded; many full/lint jobs were intentionally skipped. Clean-head `go test -race ./...` for the encounter module passed.
- Copilot’s two substantive #924 comments were fixed in `095e6f5`, but both GitHub review threads remain marked unresolved. No approval review decision is recorded.
- #923’s canonical triplet has a stale Task-3 statement saying phase-2 failure atomically aborts ([plan.md:46–53](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/9fa14c5fe47ed7752b94a49087201a3d16ab6f6b/docs/ideas/encounter-transitions/plan.md#L46-L53)); the design and implementation correctly say execution failures skip ([design.md:79–86](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/blob/9fa14c5fe47ed7752b94a49087201a3d16ab6f6b/docs/ideas/encounter-transitions/design.md#L79-L86)). Fix before calling it canonical ratification.

### Thin honest API seam after repairs

API may: load/save the opaque aggregate once, reattach non-nil decider providers, authenticate, call toolkit verbs/Pump on activity, and project toolkit-owned view/change batches.

It cannot honestly yet project the required existing wire knowledge model without inventing semantics: toolkit still needs a total per-cell observer projection plus stable change batch. It also needs a Kirk decision on absolute-route ownership: #793 says API keeps stitching/pathing, but that conflicts with the Boundary Rule if API must choose room transitions/path behavior. #924 provides transition execution, not the route-intent owner.
